goldenPoints: Tension pneumothorax: immediate needle decompression, then intercostal drain
Verbal response 1 on GCS means no verbal response at all
Surest sign of wound dehiscence: serosanguineous (salmon-coloured) discharge from the wound
Calcium oxalate is the most common renal stone
Prostate cancer spreads to lumbar vertebrae through Batson's venous plexus
Leaf-like architecture in a large breast lump = phyllodes tumour
Papillary thyroid cancer: radiation exposure, BRAF and RET/PTC mutations, psammoma bodies
Charcot triad of cholangitis: pain, fever with rigors, jaundice
Meckel diverticulum follows the rule of 2s
Graft between identical twins is an isograft
intro: Surgery carries 32 of the 300 FMGE questions, and the stems are remarkably repetitive: trauma priorities, named signs, 'most common' facts, investigation of choice, and classic image descriptions. These notes collect that exact ground — signs, triads, grades and first steps — in fact-line form for last-days revision.

subject: Surgery
tagline: Trauma priorities, named signs, triads and 'most common' facts — Surgery's 32 FMGE questions reward pattern recognition

topics.askedAs: first step in the unstable trauma patient
topics.oneLiner: Tension pneumothorax kills first — needle it, then drain it.
points: Tension pneumothorax: hyper-resonance, absent breath sounds, hypotension — immediate needle decompression at the 2nd intercostal space, then ICD
Unstable patient with positive FAST after RTA: emergency laparotomy
Haemorrhagic shock: cold extremities, tachycardia, low CVP; control bleeding and give blood products early
Rapid large-volume infusion needs a wide-bore cannula: 14G (orange) or 16G (grey)
Avoid hypotonic fluids in head injury — they worsen cerebral oedema; isotonic fluids are preferred
Pelvic fracture with membranous urethral rupture: suprapubic catheterisation first, no per-urethral catheter
Seat-belt injury most commonly injures the small bowel and its mesentery
Splenic injury in a stable child/young patient: non-operative management is preferred
topics.title: Trauma & ATLS Priorities
topics.trap: A chest X-ray is not the first step in tension pneumothorax — it is a clinical diagnosis treated before imaging.

topics.oneLiner: Cold patient + bleeding = haemorrhagic shock; stored blood gives potassium up, calcium down.
points: Haemorrhagic shock is the first shock class with falling urine output and cold peripheries
Massive transfusion complications: hyperkalaemia, hypocalcaemia, hypothermia, dilutional coagulopathy
Citrate in stored blood chelates calcium — hypocalcaemia is expected, hypokalaemia is not the classic finding
TURP syndrome: absorption of hypotonic irrigation fluid causes dilutional hyponatraemia and confusion
Postoperative hypotension with a distended abdomen: suspect intra-abdominal bleeding until disproved
qSOFA components: respiratory rate ≥22, altered mentation, systolic BP ≤100 mmHg (bilirubin is NOT a component)
topics.title: Shock, Fluids & Transfusion
topics.trap: Students pick hypokalaemia for massive transfusion — stored blood leaks potassium OUT of red cells, so hyperkalaemia is correct.

topics.askedAs: GCS value / lucid interval / surgical threshold
topics.oneLiner: Lucid interval = extradural; Battle sign = mastoid bruising of basal skull fracture.
points: GCS verbal score 1 means no verbal response (no sounds at all)
Extradural haematoma: brief loss of consciousness, lucid interval, then rapid deterioration — middle meningeal artery bleed
Battle sign: bruising over the mastoid process in basal skull fracture
Large acute subdural haematoma (>30 mL volume / significant midline shift): emergency surgical evacuation
Maxillofacial trauma with airway compromise: definitive airway — surgical airway (cricothyroidotomy/tracheostomy) when oral intubation fails
GCS 8 or less: intubate to protect the airway
Raccoon eyes and CSF otorrhoea/rhinorrhoea also indicate basal skull fracture
topics.title: Head Injury & GCS
topics.trap: Verbal 1 is silence, not incomprehensible sounds — incomprehensible sounds score 2.

topics.oneLiner: Head and neck 9%, each arm 9%, each leg 18% — in an adult.
points: Rule of 9s (adult): head and neck 9%, each upper limb 9%, each leg 18%, trunk 36%, perineum 1%
In a 3-year-old, head and neck plus one full arm ≈ 9 + 9 = 18% + head proportion is larger in children — Lund–Browder chart is used for accuracy
Parkland formula: 4 mL × body weight (kg) × % TBSA of crystalloid in the first 24 hours, half in the first 8 hours
Deep partial-thickness (deep second-degree) burns are relatively painless and heal with scarring — 'painless' is the tested fact
Electrical burns with red urine: myoglobinuria from muscle necrosis (rhabdomyolysis)
Pressure sores develop when interface pressure exceeds capillary closing pressure (~32 mmHg)
topics.title: Burns & Pressure Sores
topics.trap: The rule of 9s changes in children — the head is proportionally much larger, which is why the Lund–Browder chart exists.

topics.askedAs: breast lump → diagnosis / prognosis / drug to avoid
topics.oneLiner: Mobile rubbery lump in a young woman = fibroadenoma; leaf-like = phyllodes.
points: Fibroadenoma: firm, mobile, painless lump ('breast mouse') in a young woman — benign
Phyllodes tumour: large lump with increased stromal cellularity and leaf-like architecture on histology
Tubular carcinoma has the most favourable prognosis among invasive breast cancers
Anthracyclines (doxorubicin) are cardiotoxic — avoid in a breast cancer patient with heart failure
Post-mastectomy arm lymphoedema with purple vascular nodules = Stewart–Treves syndrome (lymphangiosarcoma)
Breast abscess in a lactating woman that fails aspiration and antibiotics: incision and drainage
Inflammatory breast cancer presents with peau d'orange and is aggressive — not a benign mastitis picture
topics.title: Breast Diseases & Cancer
topics.trap: A lactating breast abscess with fluctuation that keeps recurring after aspiration needs formal drainage — repeated aspiration alone is the wrong answer.

topics.oneLiner: Radiation + BRAF + psammoma bodies = papillary carcinoma.
points: Papillary carcinoma: most common thyroid cancer; linked to radiation exposure, RET/PTC rearrangements and BRAF mutation
Psammoma bodies and Orphan Annie eye nuclei are seen in papillary carcinoma
After total thyroidectomy for papillary cancer: radioactive iodine ablation and TSH suppression with thyroxine are the standard follow-up strategy
Medullary carcinoma arises from parafollicular C cells and secretes calcitonin; associated with MEN 2
Parathyroid adenoma is the most common cause of primary hyperparathyroidism; treatment is surgical excision of the adenoma
Follicular carcinoma spreads haematogenously to bone and lung; it cannot be diagnosed on FNAC alone
Anaplastic carcinoma: elderly patient, rapidly growing hard mass, worst prognosis
topics.title: Thyroid & Parathyroid Surgery
topics.trap: FNAC cannot separate follicular adenoma from carcinoma — capsular/vascular invasion on histology decides.

topics.oneLiner: Pain + fever + jaundice = Charcot triad = ascending cholangitis.
points: Charcot triad of acute cholangitis: right upper quadrant pain, fever with chills, and jaundice
Reynolds pentad adds hypotension and altered sensorium to the Charcot triad
Mirizzi syndrome: stone impacted in the cystic duct compresses the common hepatic duct, causing obstructive jaundice
Courvoisier law: a palpable, non-tender gallbladder with jaundice is unlikely to be due to stones — think malignancy
Asymptomatic small gallbladder polyp (<10 mm) without stones: surveillance ultrasound, not immediate surgery
Most common post-cholecystectomy problem asked: biliary injury/leak and retained CBD stone present with pain, fever and a subhepatic collection
Grey Turner sign (flank discoloration) and Cullen sign (periumbilical) indicate haemorrhagic pancreatitis
topics.title: Hepatobiliary & Gallstone Disease
topics.trap: Mirizzi is compression by a cystic-duct stone, not a stone inside the CBD — that distinction is the question.

topics.oneLiner: Grey Turner = flank bruising of haemorrhagic pancreatitis.
points: Grey Turner sign is observed in acute haemorrhagic pancreatitis
Puestow procedure: longitudinal pancreaticojejunostomy for a dilated duct in chronic pancreatitis
After pancreatic surgery, early enteral (jejunal) feeding is the preferred nutrition route
Acute pancreatitis severity is classically graded with Ranson or Glasgow criteria and APACHE II
Pancreatic pseudocyst complicates pancreatitis after about 4 weeks and has no epithelial lining
Whipple procedure (pancreaticoduodenectomy) is done for periampullary and pancreatic head tumours
topics.title: Pancreas & Spleen
topics.trap: A pseudocyst has NO epithelial lining — that single fact separates it from cystic neoplasms in options.

topics.oneLiner: Liquids harder than solids + bird-beak = achalasia.
points: Achalasia cardia: dysphagia more for liquids than solids; barium swallow shows a smooth bird-beak narrowing
Barrett oesophagus: squamocolumnar junction migrates proximally (intestinal metaplasia) after chronic reflux
Perforated peptic ulcer: sudden severe pain with a board-like rigid abdomen — resuscitate and operate
After gastrectomy, vitamin B12 malabsorption leads to megaloblastic (pernicious-type) anaemia
Highly selective vagotomy carries the highest duodenal ulcer recurrence rate among vagotomy procedures
Mallory–Weiss tear: retching/vomiting followed by haematemesis, classically after an alcohol binge
Dumping syndrome follows gastric surgery: early vasomotor symptoms after meals
topics.title: Oesophagus, Stomach & Peptic Ulcer
topics.trap: Vagotomy questions test recurrence: truncal vagotomy + drainage recurs least; highly selective vagotomy recurs most.

topics.askedAs: rule of 2s / biopsy finding → bowel disease
topics.oneLiner: Meckel = rule of 2s; crypt abscess + continuous rectum-up disease = ulcerative colitis.
points: Meckel diverticulum: rule of 2s — 2% of people, ~2 feet from the ileocaecal valve, ~2 inches long, presents by 2 years
Ulcerative colitis: continuous inflammation starting in the rectum, crypt abscesses on biopsy, mucosa only
Crohn disease: skip lesions, transmural inflammation, perianal fistulae, non-caseating granulomas
Anal squamous cell carcinoma: chemoradiation (Nigro protocol) is the primary treatment, not upfront surgery
Meigs syndrome: ovarian fibroma with ascites and pleural effusion (hydrothorax) that resolve after tumour removal
Mesenteric cyst: soft fluctuant mass mobile perpendicular to the line of mesenteric attachment
topics.title: Intestine, Colorectal & Meckel Diverticulum
topics.trap: Meigs syndrome's effusion disappears after removing the fibroma — options offering permanent pleural disease are traps.

topics.oneLiner: Salmon-coloured discharge from a post-op wound = burst abdomen until proved otherwise.
points: Surest sign of wound dehiscence: serosanguineous (salmon-coloured) discharge from the wound
Indirect inguinal hernia passes through the deep ring, lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels; it can descend into the scrotum
Direct inguinal hernia bulges through Hesselbach triangle and rarely enters the scrotum
Large incisional hernia management: repair with mesh (component separation for very large defects)
Strangulated hernia: painful, irreducible, tender swelling with obstructive features — emergency surgery
Psoas abscess: flank pain and fever with pain on passive hip extension (psoas sign), classically from spinal TB spread
topics.title: Hernia & Abdominal Wall
topics.trap: Dehiscence questions: loops of bowel seen is dramatic, but the EARLIEST/surest sign asked is the salmon-coloured discharge.

topics.oneLiner: Fistula-in-ano: MRI pelvis is the investigation of choice.
points: Fistula-in-ano: intermittent pus and blood discharge from a perianal external opening
Investigation of choice for fistula-in-ano: MRI of the pelvis/perineum
Goodsall rule: external opening behind the transverse anal line → tract curves to the posterior midline; anterior openings run radially
Perianal abscess results from infection of an anal gland in the intersphincteric plane
Appendicitis in a young woman: ultrasound is the preferred first investigation to also exclude gynaecological causes
Grade IV haemorrhoids are irreducible prolapsed piles; grades I–II are managed conservatively/banding
Thrombosed external haemorrhoid presents as acute painful perianal swelling
topics.title: Perianal Disease & Appendix
topics.trap: Goodsall rule flips at the transverse anal line — anterior openings are radial, posterior openings curve to the midline.

topics.askedAs: most common stone / node group / spread route
topics.oneLiner: Prostate cancer reaches the spine through Batson plexus — that is why the mets are vertebral and osteoblastic.
points: Calcium oxalate is the most common renal stone overall
Prostate cancer spreads to lumbar vertebrae via Batson venous plexus; metastases are osteoblastic
Testicular tumours spread first to para-aortic (lumbar) lymph nodes, not inguinal nodes
Muscle-invasive bladder cancer: radical cystectomy is the standard definitive management
10 cm RCC confined to the kidney: radical nephrectomy
Ectopic ureter in a girl: continuous dribbling despite normal voiding from birth
Hydrocele: swelling separate from the testis that transilluminates; varicocele feels like a bag of worms and does not transilluminate
Blood at the urethral meatus after perineal trauma: suspect urethral injury — do NOT pass a catheter
Benign prostatic hyperplasia arises in the transition (periurethral) zone; cancer arises in the peripheral zone
topics.title: Urology: Stones, Prostate, Testis & Bladder
topics.trap: Inguinal nodes drain the scrotal SKIN, not the testis — testicular tumours go to para-aortic nodes.

topics.oneLiner: Most common peripheral aneurysm = popliteal; gas gangrene organism = Clostridium perfringens.
points: Most common peripheral artery aneurysm: popliteal artery aneurysm
Graft between genetically identical twins is an isograft; between different species is a xenograft
Gas gangrene: crepitus with a reddish-brown wound after crush injury — Clostridium perfringens
Branchial cyst: painless fluctuant swelling at the anterior border of sternocleidomastoid in a young patient
Trotter triad in nasopharyngeal carcinoma: conductive deafness, palatal paralysis, trigeminal neuralgia
Facial nerve is the nerve at risk in parotid surgery; its marginal mandibular branch is the most commonly injured
Most common primary source of brain metastases: lung cancer
Venous ulcer: shallow ulcer over the medial malleolus in a leg with varicose veins; arterial ulcers are punched-out and distal
Dohlman procedure is done for Zenker diverticulum (pharyngeal pouch)
topics.title: Vascular, Grafts & Surgical Favourites
topics.trap: Zenker questions appear under both ENT and surgery — Dohlman is the endoscopic stapling/diverticulotomy answer.
